pipeline: # The text algebra as data. A stack of stages over a coalescing writer, a
# script of operations on the outermost stage, and the chunks the writer
#   pipeline  JSON object, read RAW; empty is {}. budget: the coalescing
#             (absent for none); stages: outermost first, each
#   ops       JSON array, read RAW: a string is a fragment written to the
#             markers (the outermost stage must be a join or concat);
#   expected  JSON array of the chunks the writer received, one per write
#             call, in order, after the last operation. Nothing is flushed
#             for the row: what is still buffered is not in the result. Or
#             ERROR:<CODE> for the first failing operation.
# Coalescing: a fragment that would overflow the buffer flushes it first; a
# fragment at least as large as the budget goes to the writer directly; a
# budget of 0 writes every non-empty fragment as it arrives.
# The output limit counts UTF-8 bytes, buffered as well as written, and
# fails before the fragment that would exceed it.
# Join: the separator goes before every item but the first, never between
# the fragments of one item; an empty item is still an item; a fragment
# outside an item is an item of its own.
# Concat: a join with no separator; the markers behave as join's.
# ReplaceText: str::replace's left-to-right, non-overlapping matches however
# the text is chunked; the bounded carry is written at a flush, which is a
# boundary no match spans; an empty literal is the identity.
# Stacks: stages compose, outermost first; the limit sees the bytes that reach the writer.
